sections.html:
Think of two desks. One decides what your house is worth, and that is the Assessor. The other mails the bill and takes your check, and that is the Treasurer, who then hands the money to the taxing districts. Neither desk sets your rate.

Lawmakers in Denver fix the assessment rate. Every school, fire, water and sanitation, library and special district then picks its own mill levy each year, which explains why neighbors across a district line can see different totals. The Treasurer sends county-collected revenue to more than 300 local taxing entities each month.

OfficeAddress and phoneRole
Treasurer1675 W. Garden of the Gods Rd., Suite 2100, Colorado Springs; (719) 520-7900Bills, collects, issues Certificates of Taxes Due, runs the tax lien sale
Assessor1675 W. Garden of the Gods Rd., Suite 2300; (719) 520-6600Values property, takes appeals, keeps mailing addresses

The Treasurer is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and closes on legal holidays. Mail payments to P.O. Box 2018, Colorado Springs, CO 80901-2018.

You have a choice: split the bill or pay it once. Half is due at the end of February, the other half June 15, and anyone paying everything at once has until April 30. When a deadline falls on a weekend or legal holiday, the next business day counts.

The bill is for last year, since Colorado collects in arrears, and it arrives in January. Before the September cutoff described below, a payment is on time if the office holds it by the deadline or the postmark is dated no later than the deadline.

  • January 10: the Assessor hands the tax warrant to the Treasurer.
  • January 28: the last day for statements to be mailed.
  • June 15: second half due. Whatever remains unpaid after this date is delinquent.
  • July: delinquency letters, plus interest and added charges.
  • September: the Treasurer advertises the unpaid real estate accounts.
  • After September 30: only cash or certified funds. A personal check or a postmark will not do.
  • October: the auction.

Unpaid real estate tax ends up at an October lien auction. Any account still carrying a balance in late October joins that year's sale. What an investor buys is the lien, so you keep the right to redeem it.

Ask for a payoff figure at (719) 520-7900. To redeem, your payment has to be in the Treasurer's hands by the last business day of the month. A lien nobody redeems can eventually lead to a treasurer's deed.

If you know about a lien, either pay it off or plan for the payoff at closing. The tax certificate from the Treasurer shows where the account stands today and any amount still owed.

sections.h2: How El Paso County values homes
sections.html:
Every odd-numbered year the state reappraises all real property, and a Notice of Valuation reaches El Paso County owners soon after May 1. Values from 2025 carry through tax year 2026, and they rest on a base year of 2023.

With 283,492 active real property parcels in 2023, mobile homes included, the office relies on mass appraisal. Houses must be valued by the market approach under state law, so a flat price per square foot is not allowed. Staff watch permits for new garages, decks, finished basements and additions, and they note demolitions and fires that cut value.

The sales that fed the 2025 and 2026 values ran from January 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024. Anything that sold later will not move your value until the next reappraisal.

You can appeal from May 1 to June 8. Options include the online property record search, a phone call, the mail, a fax or a visit. Turn over the Notice of Valuation and you will find the official appeal form on the back.

  • The 10-digit parcel number sits at the upper left of the notice.
  • Each parcel needs its own filing and its own set of papers, even when the evidence is the same.
  • Useful evidence: a recent appraisal, photos, comparable sales, or a written account of the home's condition.
  • Give the office everything you are relying on at the time you file.
  • If you mail it, keep proof.

You get a written Notice of Determination from the Assessor by August 15. Still unhappy? Take it to the County Board of Equalization at 1675 W. Garden of the Gods Road. Beyond that board sit three routes: the Board of Assessment Appeals, district court, or binding arbitration with the county commissioners. Start any of them within 30 days of the Board of Equalization's decision letter. Arbitration results cannot be challenged.

sections.h2: Tax paperwork for selling a house
sections.html:
The main document is a Certificate of Taxes Due, which shows whether taxes on a parcel are owed or paid. The Treasurer charges $10 per certificate.

  • Title and settlement companies usually subscribe to the county's CTD portal: $500 to set up, $500 each year to renew, and $10 per certificate.
  • Anyone else can mail the request form with a $10 check payable to El Paso County Treasurer, Attn: Tax Certificates.
  • Allow 48 hours of processing once the office receives a mailed request.

Online search covers just the current billing cycle and can miss older balances or special assessments billed afterward, so order the certificate. When a signed certificate shows all taxes paid and all tax sales redeemed, it is conclusive proof the parcel was clear of property taxes on that date.

You can pay through the county's online portal or send a check. EquaPay spreads prepayment over monthly installments, and the Treasurer's electronic delivery form switches you to emailed statements.

Statements follow the mailing address the Assessor has on file. After a move or sale, file the Assessor's change of address form and the Treasurer picks it up automatically. The Tax History Dashboard offers public access to past records.

Prepaying next year's tax? It has to arrive by noon on the last business day of December. Later payments carry a January receipt date.

Owing tax does not stop a sale. Here is how it normally plays out.

  1. Your title company requests the Certificate of Taxes Due.
  2. It lists what is owed this cycle. A lien already sold? Phone (719) 520-7900 for the payoff.
  3. Closing pays the balance out of your proceeds.
  4. The Treasurer logs the payment and the account clears.

A cash buyer goes through the same steps. What changes is that showings and lender conditions drop away, which leaves the tax payoff as one of the few items to settle. Value, classification and appeals go to the Assessor at (719) 520-6600. Payments, statements, liens and certificates go to the Treasurer.

sections.h2: El Paso County at a glance
sections.html: The county covers 2,127 square miles of land, from the Pikes Peak foothills in the west to farm and ranch land in the east. Population was 730,395 in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 757,040. Agricultural land sits mostly in the east and must meet strict criteria for that classification, while mountain parcels can be affected by topography and access.

faqs.q: When are El Paso County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half is due the last day of February and half June 15, or the whole amount by April 30. Weekend and holiday dates roll to the next business day.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal an El Paso County valuation?
faqs.a: June 8 is the last day. The window opens May 1, right after notices go out, and the Assessor answers by August 15.

faqs.q: How much is a Certificate of Taxes Due in El Paso County?
faqs.a: The fee is $10 for each certificate. Mail a check with every request and give the office 48 hours to process it.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the June 15 payment?
faqs.a: The account turns delinquent. Letters, interest and charges follow in July, advertising in September and the lien auction in October.

faqs.q: Can I sell my El Paso County house if taxes are owed?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company orders the certificate, the balance appears on it, and closing pays it. If a lien was sold, ask the Treasurer at (719) 520-7900 for the payoff.
